overview: After 1.b3 Nf6 2.Bb2 g6, White plays 3.g4, the Spike, grabbing kingside space and threatening g5 to kick the knight away from the long diagonal. Black cannot take on g4 because Bxh8 follows once the f6 knight moves, so Black plays 3...Bg7 or ...d5 and counters in the centre. White's king is loosened, so the game is double-edged.

white_ideas.idea: Push g5 to drive the knight away and open the long diagonal
Play Bg2, Nf3 and d3 or e3, supported by the b2 bishop
Use space on the kingside and keep the king flexible

black_ideas.idea: Develop ...Bg7 and attack the loosened g4 with ...d5 and ...h5
Strike with ...c5 and ...d5 in the centre

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on b3, g4 against Black fianchetto on g7
Flexible centre with long diagonals contested

character.notes: The early g4 loosens White and invites mutual attacks and sharp tactics.

gambit.notes: No pawn is given: 3...Nxg4 fails to Bxh8 and the position stays even in material.

soundness.notes: Playable and played by Larsen, though it weakens the king.

structure.notes: The centre is undecided and flank pawns decide the middlegame.

approach.notes: Rarely played by strong players and chosen for surprise.

level.notes: Plans need care but the theory is small.
